command_words.Show that: Prove a given result; every step must be shown (answer given).
command_words.Hence: Use the previous result to reach the answer.
command_words.Hence or otherwise: Using the previous result is expected, but any valid method earns the marks.
command_words.Find: Work out; method marks need working.
command_words.Calculate: Work out from given facts; show working.
command_words.Sketch: Draw the shape with key features labelled (intercepts, asymptotes, turning points), not to scale.
command_words.Exact: Give the answer in surd, fraction, pi or ln form, not a decimal.
command_words.Verify: Show that given values satisfy the statement.
command_words.Interpret: Explain the meaning of a result in the context of the question.

kcs.title: Simplifying rational expressions
kcs.statement: Simplification of rational expressions including factorising and cancelling, and algebraic division.
kcs.raw: Simplification of rational expressions including factorising and cancelling, and algebraic division.
kcs.guidance: Denominators of rational expressions will be linear or quadratic, e.g. $\dfrac{1}{ax+b}$, $\dfrac{x^3+1}{px^2+qx+r}$, $\dfrac{x-1}{x^2}$.

kcs.title: Functions, domain, range and inverses
kcs.statement: Definition of a function. Domain and range of functions. Composition of functions. Inverse functions and their graphs.
kcs.raw: Definition of a function. Domain and range of functions. Composition of functions. Inverse functions and their graphs.
kcs.guidance: The concept of a function as a one-one or many-one mapping from $\mathbb{R}$ (or a subset of $\mathbb{R}$) to $\mathbb{R}$ will be used. The notation $f:x \mapsto f(x)$ may be used. Students should know that $fg$ means 'do $g$ first, then $f$'. Students should know that if $f^{-1}$ exists, then $f^{-1}f(x) = ff^{-1}(x) = x$.

kcs.title: The modulus function
kcs.guidance: Students should be able to sketch the graphs of $y=|ax+b|$ and the graphs of $y=|f(x)|$ and $y=f(|x|)$, given the graph of $y=f(x)$. For example, sketch the graph with equation $y=|2x-1|$ and use the graph to solve the equation $|2x-1|=x+5$ or the inequality $|2x-1|>x+5$.

kcs.title: Combined graph transformations
kcs.statement: Combinations of the transformations $y=f(x)$ as represented by $y=af(x)$, $y=f(x)+a$, $y=f(x+a)$, $y=f(ax)$.
kcs.raw: Combinations of the transformations y = f(x) as represented by y = af(x), y = f(x) + a, y = f(x + a), y = f(ax).
kcs.guidance: Students should be able to sketch the graph of, for example, $y=2f(3x)$, $y=f(-x)+1$, given the graph of $y=f(x)$, or the graph of, for example, $y=3+\sin 2x$, $y=-\cos\left(x+\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$. The graph of $y=f(ax+b)$ will not be required.

kcs.title: Reciprocal and inverse trig functions
kcs.statement: Knowledge of secant, cosecant and cotangent and of arcsin, arccos and arctan. Their relationships to sine, cosine and tangent. Understanding of their graphs and appropriate restricted domains.
kcs.raw: Knowledge of secant, cosecant and cotangent and of arcsin, arccos and arctan. Their relationships to sine, cosine and tangent. Understanding of their graphs and appropriate restricted domains.
kcs.guidance: Angles measured in both degrees and radians.

kcs.title: Sec² and cosec² identities
kcs.raw: Knowledge and use of sec2 θ = 1 + tan2 θ  and cosec2 θ = 1 + cot2 θ.

kcs.title: Compound and double angle formulae
kcs.statement: Knowledge and use of double angle formulae; use of formulae for $\sin(A \pm B)$, $\cos(A \pm B)$ and $\tan(A \pm B)$ and of expressions for $a\cos\theta+b\sin\theta$ in the equivalent forms of $r\cos(\theta \pm \alpha)$ or $r\sin(\theta \pm \alpha)$.
kcs.raw: Knowledge and use of double angle formulae; use of formulae for sin (A ± B), cos (A ± B) and tan (A ± B) and of expressions for a cos θ + b sin θ in the equivalent forms of r cos (θ  ± a) or r sin (θ ± a).
kcs.guidance: To include application to half angles. Knowledge of the $t=\tan\frac{1}{2}\theta$ formulae will not be required. Students should be able to solve equations such as $a\cos\theta+b\sin\theta=c$ in a given interval, and to prove identities such as $\cos x\cos 2x+\sin x\sin 2x \equiv \cos x$.

kcs.title: The exponential function e^x
kcs.raw: The function ex and its graph.
kcs.guidance: To include the graph of $y=e^{ax+b}+c$. Solution of equations of the form $e^{ax+b}=p$ and

kcs.title: The natural logarithm ln x
kcs.statement: The function $\ln x$ and its graph; $\ln x$ as the inverse function of $e^x$.
kcs.raw: The function ln x and its graph; ln x as the inverse function of ex.

kcs.title: Using logarithmic graphs to fit models
kcs.statement: Use logarithmic graphs to estimate parameters in relationships of the form $y=ax^n$ and $y=kb^x$.
kcs.raw: Use logarithmic graphs to estimate parameters in relationships of the form y = axn and y = kbx.
kcs.guidance: Plot $\log y$ against $\log x$ and obtain a straight line where the intercept is $\log a$ and the gradient is $n$. Plot $\log y$ against $x$ and obtain a straight line where the intercept is $\log k$ and the gradient is $\log b$.

kcs.title: Differentiating exponential, log and trig functions
kcs.statement: Differentiation of $e^{kx}$, $\ln kx$, $\sin kx$, $\cos kx$, $\tan kx$ and their sums and differences.
kcs.raw: Differentiation of ekx, ln kx, sin kx, cos kx, tan kx and their sums and differences.

kcs.title: Product, quotient and chain rules
kcs.statement: Differentiation using the product rule, the quotient rule and the chain rule.
kcs.raw: Differentiation using the product rule, the quotient rule and the chain rule.
kcs.guidance: Differentiation of $\csc x$, $\cot x$ and $\sec x$ is required. Skill will be expected in the differentiation of functions generated from standard functions using products, quotients and composition, such as $3e^x\sin x$, $\dfrac{2x^4}{\cos x}$, $\cos(x^2)$ and $\tan^2 2x$.

kcs.title: Exponential growth and decay
kcs.statement: Understand and use exponential growth and decay.
kcs.raw: Understand and use exponential growth and decay.
kcs.guidance: Students should be familiar with terms such as 'initial', meaning when $t=0$. Students may need to explore the behaviour for large values of $t$ or to consider whether the range of values predicted is appropriate. Consideration of a second, improved model may be required. Knowledge and use of the result $\dfrac{d}{dx}(a^x) = a^x \ln a$ is expected.

kcs.title: Integrating exponential, log and trig functions
kcs.statement: Integration of $e^{kx}$, $\dfrac{1}{nx}$, $\sin kx$, $\cos kx$ and their sums and differences.
kcs.raw: Integration of ekx, 1 nx , sin kx, cos kx and their sums and differences.
kcs.guidance: To include integration of standard functions such as $\sin 3x$, $e^{5x}$, $\dfrac{1}{2x}$.

kcs.title: Integration by recognition
kcs.statement: Integration by recognition of known derivatives to include integrals of the form $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{f'(x)}{f(x)}\,dx = \ln|f(x)|+c$ and $\displaystyle\int f'(x)[f(x)]^n\,dx = \dfrac{[f(x)]^{n+1}}{n+1}+c$.
kcs.raw: Integration by recognition of known derivatives to include integrals of the form ′∫ f ( ) x d x = ln (f(x)) + c and f ( ) x = [ ] 1 n + ′∫ f ( ) x n + c f ( )[f ( )] d x x x n + 1
kcs.guidance: For example, to include integration of $\tan x$, $\sec^2 2x$. Students are expected to be able to use trigonometric identities to integrate, for example, $\sin^2 x$, $\tan^2 x$, $\cos^2 3x$.

kcs.title: Locating roots by sign change
kcs.statement: Location of roots of $f(x) = 0$ by considering changes of sign of $f(x)$ in an interval of $x$ in which $f(x)$ is continuous.
kcs.raw: Location of roots of f(x) = 0 by considering changes of sign of f(x) in an interval of x in which f(x) is continuous.

kcs.title: Iterative methods for equations
kcs.statement: Approximate solution of equations using simple iterative methods, including recurrence relations of the form $x_{n+1}=f(x_n)$.
kcs.raw: Approximate solution of equations using simple iterative methods, including recurrence relations of the form xn + 1 = f(xn)
kcs.guidance: Solution of equations by use of iterative procedures, for which leads will be given.
